title: Pip and the Unsent Bubble
summary: Pip the bubble courier has forty unpopped deliveries behind him. His next parcel, from a lantern keeper to her granddaughter before a tap dance, seems to be empty. His attempt to fill it with good luck nearly takes the bandstand with it.
coverAlt: Pip, a round yellow chick in a blue mail cap and red satchel, runs beneath an enormous empty silvery speech bubble. Dot stands in red tap shoes on a striped bandstand beside Nan. The bubbly title fills the sky.
style: Bubblegum-pop cel cartoon with springy indigo brushwork, bright gouache colors, and illustrated two-panel comedy timing.

pages.alt: Pip races past a blue mailbox under a bright sky. His cap catches a loose bubble just before it lands.
pages.transcript:
Pip: Parcel, parcel, bubble for the baker!

Pip: Caught it. That makes forty deliveries without a pop.

pages.alt: Nan steadies the lantern winch above the bandstand and leans down to Pip. She passes him a clear, pearly bubble and taps its surface.
pages.transcript:
Nan: I have to keep these lanterns up. Take this to Dot before her first dance.

Nan: Two taps, Pip. Then hold it still.

pages.alt: Pip peers through the empty bubble until his beak looks enormous. On a bench, he listens to it like a seashell.
pages.transcript:
Pip: Hello in there? I can see the back of my beak.

Pip: Nothing. I must have dropped the words.

pages.alt: Pip searches his coral mailbag with his feet in the air. At the echo kiosk he poises the bubble beside a big brass horn.
pages.transcript:
Pip: Lint. A bent spoon. Last Tuesday’s biscuit. No words.

Pip: Dot’s about to dance. I can think of something encouraging.

pages.alt: Pip calls into the horn. Pink noise swirls into the bubble until it swells and pulls the little courier sideways.
pages.transcript:
Pip: GOOD LUCK! Give it some bounce! Knock their socks off!

Pip: That seems like enough luck for one frog. Whoa!

pages.alt: The swollen bubble catches in striped bunting. From a blue stool Pip frees the string as the lanterns sway.
pages.transcript:
Pip: Excuse me. My message appears to be wearing your awning.

Pip: There! No pops. Only one small incident with a building.

pages.alt: Backstage, Dot sits on a trunk in her red tap shoes. The loud pink parcel nudges a cymbal while Pip tries to hand it to her.
pages.transcript:
Dot: My knees are keeping time all by themselves.

Pip: Special delivery from Nan! Mind the cym—

pages.alt: Dot covers her ears as the cymbal rings. Pip lowers himself onto the trunk beside her and stops talking.
pages.transcript:
Dot: Everyone keeps saying, “Do your best.” What if my best is very small?

Pip: I put those words in there. Nan didn’t send them.

pages.alt: Through the curtains Pip watches Nan at the lantern rail. He holds his wing against the bubble and feels a faint ripple.
pages.transcript:
Pip: Look at her hand. Tap, tap … and then she leaves it there.

Pip: That’s what she did when she gave me this. I hardly let her finish.

pages.alt: Pip loosens the bubble’s tail at an open window. The pink noise escapes. He takes off his cap and brings the smaller, clear bubble back to Dot.
pages.transcript:
Pip: Out you go, socks. You too, enormous luck.

Pip: I can send it back, Dot. Or we can try it Nan’s way.

pages.alt: Dot lays one hand on the bubble while Pip taps the opposite side twice. Both hold still, palms against its clear skin.
pages.transcript:
Dot: Let me feel it.

Dot: Oh. Two little taps and a long, warm hand. That’s how Nan says, “I’m here.”

pages.alt: Dot spots Nan in the lantern gallery. Facing the open stage, she sets her red shoes together while Pip holds the curtain.
pages.transcript:
Dot: We made that up when I was too little to see her from the stage.

Dot: I know how to start. You can leave the big horn here.

pages.alt: Dot takes two light steps onto the stage. In the wing, Pip tips the announcing horn down and listens.
pages.transcript:
Dot: Tap. Tap.

Pip: The quiet bit is part of it. You have to give it room.

pages.alt: Dot balances on one red shoe. Pip taps the stage edge with both wings. The bandstand audience claps as Nan watches from the lantern gallery.
pages.transcript:
Dot: There you are, Nan.

Nan: There you are, love.

pages.alt: Dot hugs Nan beside the bandstand. Pip clasps his wings beneath the floating parcel. At the blue mailbox he hugs his red delivery book under the evening lights.
pages.transcript:
Nan: Did my message arrive?

Pip: Received in full. I had to take a few things out first.
